sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:238136
Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 25126 of 2023

Applicant :- Devendra Yadav
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others

Counsel for Applicant :- Rayoof Ali,Sami Ullah Khan
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Beena Mishra

Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Rejoinder affidavit filed today on behalf of the applicant, is taken on record.
2.  Sri Ghanshyam Mishra, learned Brief Holder apprised the Court that on 27.5.2023 notice has been served to the informant.
Despite service of notice, none appeared on behalf of the informant.
Even Ms. Beena Mishra, learned counsel for the High Court Legal Services Committee is not present.
3. Heard Sri Sami Ullah Khan, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Ghanshyam Mishra, learned Brief Holder for the State-respondent.

4. The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
75 of 2023, under Sections 354, 341, 294, 376, 506 IPC and Section 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Harpur Budahat, District Gorakhpur, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

sentences.text:
FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant on 24.4.2023 and according to the FIR victim was aged about 17 years old and for last one year applicant was continuously harassing her and pressurized her to perform marriage with him and also prepared her obscene photographs and under the threat to viral the same forcibly made physical relationship with her.
6.
Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that on the basis of false allegation, applicant has been made accused in the present matter.

7. He further submitted that FIR of the present case appears to be based on vague facts and however, victim in her statement under section 161 Cr.P.C. repeated the version of the FIR but in the statement under section 164 Cr.P.C. she did not state that applicant committed rape upon her.
8.

He further submitted that actually victim and applicant both were having love affair with each other but unfortunately some dispute arose between both of them and thereafter victim lodged FIR of the present case and this fact is even evident from the statement of the victim recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C.
9.

He further submitted that even as per school record and ossification test report of the victim she was about 17 years old and therefore, possibility could not be ruled out that she was about 18 years old.
10. He further submitted that victim even appearance wise looks like 18 years old girl.
11. He further submitted that applicant is having no criminal history and he is in jail in the present matter since 24.4.2023 i.e. for last more than six months.

12. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the fact that victim in her statement recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C. did not make any allegation of rape against the applicant and even as per school record she was about 17 years old and in the light of her statement recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C., at this stage, it cannot be said that she was not the consenting party.
13. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

14. However, in the FIR and in the statement recorded under section 161 Cr.P.C. victim stated that applicant under the threat to viral her photograph committed rape upon her but during investigation no obscene photographs or videograph of the victim could be recovered.
15. Further, victim in her statements recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C. did not make any allegation of rape and in the light of the statement under section 164 Cr.P.C. defence taken by the applicant

,
cannot be brushed aside, at this stage.
16. Further, applicant is having no previous criminal history and he is in jail in the present matter since last more than six months.

sentences.text:
Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
18. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

19. Let the applicant-Devendra Yadav, be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
20.
In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

21. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
Order Date :- 15.12.2023 Ankita  Devendra Yadav vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192765900/
